# Incident Report — 2024-08-15 Malware Infection

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| AD domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in user account | **plucero** (LAFONTAINEBLEU\plucero, confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString) |
| DHCP server / DC | 10.8.15.4 |

## Malware Family
**Latrodectus** loader/downloader.

Attribution basis:
- **Signature-level indicator:** the second-stage binary retrieved during the infection contains an embedded PDB debug path: `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`. This internal build path/project naming ("knock") is a known artifact of Latrodectus loader builds.
- **Behavioral corroboration** (all independently observed in this capture, consistent with documented Latrodectus delivery chains): a fake shipping/invoice lure delivering a ZIP containing a single, deliberately oversized (~6.9 MB) JScript file padded with large blocks of unrelated scraped text (a known Latrodectus JS-obfuscation/anti-sandbox technique); execution of that script leading to a BITS-based (`Microsoft BITS/7.8` user agent) download of a PE32+ DLL from a bare IP address over plain HTTP; and post-execution beaconing from the DLL back to the same bare IP with encrypted HTTP request/response bodies.

Given both a build-artifact indicator and a matching behavioral chain, this is a **high-confidence but not fully signature/YARA-confirmed** identification (no AV/EDR detection artifacts or YARA scan were available in the evidence set; no internet-based reputation lookups were used).

## Timeline (all times UTC+4, as recorded in capture)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 04:09:43 | Capture start / host DHCP DISCOVER as `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` |
| 04:10:58 | `GET /managements?...` to **quote.checkfedexexp.com** (104.21.55.70) — downloads ZIP archive disguised as a FedEx shipment notice |
| ~04:11:38 | TLS session to **business.checkfedexexp.com** (172.67.170.159) — same phishing infrastructure |
| 04:11:59 | `HEAD`/`GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` via BITS to **72.5.43.29:80** — second-stage DLL download |
| 04:13:00 – 04:42:25 | Persistent `GET /` and `POST /` beaconing to **72.5.43.29:80** at ~5–7 second intervals, spoofed User-Agent `Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`, with high-entropy (encrypted) request/response bodies. Two check-ins returned a large (305,148-byte) encrypted blob, consistent with a follow-on module/plugin push; most others returned a 94-byte "no task" keepalive. |

## Indicators of Compromise

**Command-and-control**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — hardcoded-IP C2 for loader download and ongoing beaconing (no DNS lookup preceded contact, confirming it is embedded in the malware config)

**Malicious/lure domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` → 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159 (Cloudflare-fronted)

**Malicious URL**
- `hxxp://quote[.]checkfedexexp[.]com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`
- `hxxp://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`

**Transferred files / hashes**
| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `managements` (ZIP, delivered as HTTP response body, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Initial-access dropper package |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside the ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Oversized/padded JScript downloader |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (PE32+ DLL, x86-64) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | Latrodectus loader DLL; embeds PDB path `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`; internal name `release.dll`; imports `CreateMutexW`/`OpenMutexW` (mutex-gated single-instance check), `WS2_32.dll` (network) |

**Note on other observed traffic:** Requests to `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`, `acroipm2.adobe.com` (Adobe ARM update check), and OCSP/Microsoft telemetry endpoints are legitimate Windows/Adobe background activity and are **not** part of the infection chain.
